subject: PraxisAI — Private VPC procurement & allowlist next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@praxisai.co>, Priya Rao <priya@praxisai.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: PraxisAI — Private VPC procurement & allowlist next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to hear more about PraxisAI's latency and data-governance needs. Below is a short recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can move the Private VPC procurement forward.

Recap (quick):
- Deployment mode preference: Private VPC (customer-managed VPC in AWS) to satisfy data residency and SOC2 constraints.
- Two network options on the table: PrivateLink endpoint (Redwood-managed interface endpoint) vs VPC Peering (direct peering). PraxisAI prefers PrivateLink for tenant-level isolation but wants to confirm egress/CIDR handling.
- Procurement timeline: Legal + security sign-off expected by end of next week; infra team targets final networking sign-off in 2 weeks.

Action items / asks from PraxisAI (what we need from you):
1) Confirm final list of IP ranges (egress) or confirm you'll use a NAT/proxy that can present a fixed egress IPs to us. If you plan to rely on our PrivateLink, we will still need the expected source IP ranges for any support whitelisting.
2) Share preferred PrivateLink vs Peering decision and any blockers (e.g., cross-account peering constraints).
3) Provide a short networking contacts list (netops engineer + procurement PO). We need a contact who can sign off on firewall/allowlist tests.

Redwood next steps (we'll):
- Attach a network matrix template (praxis_network_matrix.xlsx) for you to fill with CIDRs, expected source ports, and traffic patterns.
- Share our Private VPC checklist (redwood_privatenet-checklist.pdf) which includes timelines for cert exchange, KMS/HSM notes, and SOC2 evidence packaging.
- Schedule a 30-min netops runbook review next week (proposal: Tue 2026-04-14 10:00 AM PDT).

Please reply with the items above or drop availability for the runbook review. If you want, we can stand up a short canary environment on Dedicated capacity while networking is finalized — that option reduces risk but requires a separate billing path.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_privatenet-checklist.pdf (pdf), praxis_network_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Samir Patel <samir@praxisai.co>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@praxisai.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PraxisAI — Private VPC procurement & allowlist next steps

Thanks, Evelyn — useful summary. Quick answers below and I've attached a draft network matrix.

1) Egress IPs: Our infra team currently publishes egress from a set of NAT gateways behind a static Elastic IP block. We'll confirm exact CIDRs but initial list is: 54.187.12.0/24, 3.229.45.128/25. We can also route through a customer proxy that will present a single IP if you prefer.
2) PrivateLink vs Peering: Preference = PrivateLink (we want interface endpoints per account for security/compliance). Main concern is that some older ops scripts expect peered VPCs; we can update those but want to confirm timing.
3) Netops contact: Priya Rao (priya@praxisai.co) — she'll own the allowlist/test sign-off. Procurement contact: Joel Nguyen <joel@praxisai.co> (CC'd in procurement thread separately).

Attachments: praxis_network_matrix.xlsx (attached)

—Samir
Samir Patel
CTO, PraxisAI
samir@praxisai.co | +1 (650) 555-0133

Samir — thanks for the quick turn. A couple clarifying points after I reviewed the excel:

- CIDRs: the two ranges look good as a starting point. We'll ask our infra team to reserve those in our allowlist table but we'll need CIDR + expected source ports. Can you mark which ranges will be used for control plane vs inference traffic? (control plane = model management, metrics; inference = token traffic).
- PrivateLink details: happy to support interface endpoints. Two notes: (1) if you want per-account interface endpoints we'll need your AWS account IDs for each environment (dev/stage/prod) so we can create the endpoints; (2) PrivateLink health checks require that we see a routable connection for TLS; we'll run a short connectivity test during cutover.
- Procurement: can you confirm Joel's PO cadence (net30/45) and if PraxisAI requires a purchase order number on invoices? We can route this to Marissa (sales ops).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Priya: fill the matrix with the columns for control vs inference traffic + AWS account IDs.
- Priya/Evelyn: run a 30-min netops screen-share on Tue 2026-04-14 10:00 AM PDT to validate connectivity and confirm PrivateLink interface naming.
- Marissa: I'll loop you on PO terms once Joel confirms cadence.

Thanks all — I'll update the HubSpot deal and drop these items into the redwood_privatenet-checklist so we track pre-procurement gating items.

Evelyn
